sources.title: Rule/list/label consistency derivation
sources.details: Hand reasoning, not model execution: let n=f(state) be card when the application-ID key exists, ask_id otherwise, address for the address task, undefined for unsupported tasks. In a list with known unique actions and none retained, answer n iff n is present, otherwise none. Removing only card changes membership without changing f(state). Removing the ID changes f(state). Supported-but-absent and unsupported both map to none, so none cannot identify the cause. Two candidates with identical correct meaning violate uniqueness regardless of their IDs. The same none appearing with different labels refutes the always-none rule on this pair; it cannot establish that learned models eliminate shortcuts. Related variants in two splits do not test unseen-family generalization.
